In [[algebraic geometry]], <math>\mu</math> is said to be a multiplicative [[distance]] function over a [[Field (mathematics)|field]] if it satisfies<ref>{{citation
 | last = Hartshorne | first = Robin |author-link=Robin Hartshorne
 | doi = 10.1007/978-0-387-22676-7
 | isbn = 0-387-98650-2
 | location = New York
 | mr = 1761093
 | page = 363
 | publisher = Springer-Verlag
 | series = [[Undergraduate Texts in Mathematics]]
 | title = Geometry: Euclid and beyond
 | url = https://books.google.com/books?id=EJCSL9S6la0C&pg=PA363
 | year = 2000}}.</ref>
* <math>\mu(AB)>1.\,</math>
* ''AB'' is [[congruence relation|congruent]] to A'B' [[iff]] <math>\mu(AB)=\mu(A'B').\,</math>
* ''AB'' < ''A<nowiki>'</nowiki>B<nowiki>'</nowiki>'' iff <math>\mu(AB)<\mu(A'B').\,</math>
* <math>\mu(AB+CD)=\mu(AB)\mu(CD).\,</math>
